rebar.introLead: ProBar is CBI Tunisia's Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) reinforcement bar line — engineered as a high-performance, corrosion-resistant alternative to conventional steel reinforcement, and manufactured on production lines built around optimized pultrusion technology, precision resin control and standardized quality calibration.
rebar.workflowIntro: Every ProBar reinforcement bar moves through the same disciplined production pillars that define CBI Tunisia's manufacturing platform — engineered for consistent mechanical performance and dimensional accuracy on every line.
rebar.stage1Desc: Resin formulation and flow are precisely controlled at the point of fiber impregnation, the foundation of consistent mechanical performance in every ProBar rebar.
rebar.stage2Desc: Reinforcement bars are formed on optimized pultrusion lines engineered for dimensional accuracy and repeatable output, bar after bar.
rebar.stage3Desc: Standardized calibration protocols validate every production run against consistent mechanical and dimensional benchmarks.
rebar.stage4Desc: Real-time production monitoring and preventive maintenance frameworks protect process discipline and product consistency across the full production run.
rebar.processPara1: ProBar production is built on advanced pultrusion process control, engineered and optimized specifically for GFRP reinforcement bar performance. Structured quality management systems, aligned with international standards, govern every stage of the process.
rebar.processPara2: This is not a trial-and-error operation. ProBar is manufactured on validated production protocols developed over more than 10 years of hands-on GFRP manufacturing experience — the result is faster stabilization, consistent product quality and controlled performance from the first bar produced.
rebar.diagramCaption2: Quality calibration and process control for ProBar production.
rebar.philosophyTitle: A Manufacturing Philosophy Built on Discipline
rebar.philosophyPara1: CBI Tunisia's approach to ProBar manufacturing rests on structured quality management, preventive and predictive maintenance, and standardized quality assurance systems — engineered so that industrial resilience, scalability and production consistency are present from day one, not added later.
rebar.philosophyPara2: That discipline is backed by internationally recognized certification: ISO 9001:2015 quality management, membership of iTAB and EOTA, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, and registration under the International EPD System and CNERIB.
rebar.benefit1Desc: ProBar delivers a tensile strength of ≥1000 MPa, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel reinforcement.
rebar.benefit2Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction removes the steel-reinforcement failure mode that drives most reinforced-concrete repair costs.
rebar.benefit3Desc: At approximately 75% the weight of steel, ProBar reduces logistics costs and makes on-site handling and installation easier.
rebar.benefit4Desc: A design service life of 75–100 years, against 30–50 years typical of steel, with minimal maintenance even in aggressive environments.
rebar.advantage1Desc: Process flow optimization and standardized calibration protect production consistency as output scales.
rebar.advantage2Desc: Real-time production monitoring and data-driven operational management give full visibility into every production run.
rebar.advantage3Desc: Non-conductive, chemically resistant and corrosion-free construction translates into an improved total cost of ownership over the structure's lifetime.
rebar.advantage4Desc: Civil engineering integration, technical advisory and specification development support consultants and EPC contractors from design through delivery.
rebar.seoTitle: GFRP Rebar Manufacturing by CBI Tunisia
rebar.seoPara1: ProBar is CBI Tunisia's GFRP rebar production line, purpose-built to deliver a corrosion-resistant, high-tensile alternative to steel reinforcement bars for coastal infrastructure, industrial facilities, logistics platforms and maintenance-sensitive construction projects. Manufactured with optimized pultrusion technology and precision resin control, ProBar reinforcement bars are engineered for dimensional accuracy and consistent mechanical performance, batch after batch.
rebar.seoPara2: PROBAR is not positioned as a universal replacement for steel — it is a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for the applications where corrosion resistance and lifecycle performance matter most. Backed by ISO 9001:2015, EOTA/European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, and by more than 10 years of hands-on GFRP manufacturing experience, ProBar gives engineers, consultants and EPC contractors a validated, technically supported alternative to conventional steel rebar.
rebar.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about ProBar GFRP reinforcement bars.
rebar.faqA1: ProBar reinforcement bars are manufactured under CBI Tunisia's ISO 9001:2015 quality system, with European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295 and EPD/CNERIB registration — the same certifications that apply across the company's production lines.
rebar.faqQ2: How is ProBar different from steel reinforcement bars?
rebar.faqA2: ProBar delivers ≥1000 MPa tensile strength versus 400–600 MPa for conventional steel, at roughly 75% less weight, with full corrosion resistance and a 75–100 year design service life against 30–50 years typical of steel.

mesh.introLead: ProMesh is CBI Tunisia's Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) mesh reinforcement line — manufactured on the same precision resin-control and quality-calibration platform as ProBar, engineered for corrosion-free reinforcement in slab, panel and surface applications.
mesh.workflowIntro: ProMesh is produced on the same disciplined manufacturing pillars as every CBI Tunisia production line — precision, calibration and monitoring applied consistently across the mesh format.
mesh.stage1Desc: The same precision resin control systems used across CBI Tunisia's GFRP lines govern fiber impregnation for ProMesh, the basis of consistent mechanical performance.
mesh.stage2Desc: ProMesh is formed on optimized production lines engineered to hold consistent mesh geometry and dimensional accuracy.
mesh.stage3Desc: Every production run is validated against standardized quality calibration protocols shared with ProBar, for consistent mechanical performance.
mesh.stage4Desc: Real-time production monitoring and preventive maintenance frameworks protect process discipline throughout the run.
mesh.processPara1: ProMesh shares its production platform with ProBar — the same advanced pultrusion process control and structured quality management systems, adapted to deliver a corrosion-free composite mesh rather than a bar profile.
mesh.processPara2: Because ProMesh is manufactured on validated production protocols developed over more than 10 years of GFRP manufacturing experience, output reaches consistent product quality and controlled performance without a lengthy trial-and-error phase.
mesh.diagramCaption2: Quality calibration and process control for ProMesh production.
mesh.philosophyPara1: ProMesh is not manufactured to a separate standard from ProBar — it is built on the same structured quality management, preventive maintenance and standardized quality assurance systems, so that mesh reinforcement meets the same production discipline as CBI Tunisia's reinforcement bars.
mesh.philosophyPara2: That shared discipline is backed by the same certification framework: ISO 9001:2015, iTAB and EOTA membership, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, and registration under the International EPD System and CNERIB.
mesh.benefit1Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant GFRP construction removes the steel-mesh corrosion risk in slabs, panels and surface applications.
mesh.benefit2Desc: Manufactured on the same precision resin-control and calibration platform as ProBar, for repeatable mechanical performance across every roll.
mesh.benefit3Desc: As a GFRP composite, ProMesh is significantly lighter than steel mesh, easing transport and on-site handling.
mesh.benefit4Desc: Non-conductive and chemically resistant construction supports use in environments where steel mesh carries added risk.
mesh.advantage1Desc: Process flow optimization and standardized calibration, shared with ProBar, protect consistency across every mesh production run.
mesh.advantage2Desc: Real-time production monitoring and data-driven operational management give full visibility into mesh production.
mesh.advantage3Desc: Corrosion-free, non-conductive construction supports an improved total cost of ownership over the life of the structure.
mesh.advantage4Desc: Civil engineering integration and specification development support consultants and EPC contractors in adopting GFRP mesh with confidence.
mesh.seoTitle: GFRP Mesh Manufacturing by CBI Tunisia
mesh.seoPara1: ProMesh is CBI Tunisia's GFRP mesh production line, engineered for corrosion-free reinforcement in slabs, panels and surface applications across coastal infrastructure, industrial facilities, logistics platforms and maintenance-sensitive projects. Produced on the same optimized pultrusion technology and precision resin-control platform as ProBar, ProMesh delivers the mechanical consistency of a validated, quality-calibrated production process.
mesh.seoPara2: As with all PROBAR products, ProMesh is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution rather than a universal replacement for steel mesh. Backed by ISO 9001:2015, EOTA/ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, and by CBI Tunisia's 10+ years of GFRP manufacturing experience, ProMesh gives engineers and contractors a technically supported composite alternative for corrosion-sensitive reinforcement applications.
mesh.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about ProMesh GFRP mesh systems.
mesh.faqQ1: Is ProMesh manufactured to the same standard as ProBar?
mesh.faqA1: Yes. ProMesh is produced on the same precision resin-control and quality-calibration platform as ProBar, under the same structured quality management and standardized quality assurance systems.
mesh.faqA2: ProMesh is engineered for corrosion-free reinforcement in slab, panel and surface applications, wherever conventional steel mesh would be exposed to corrosive or maintenance-sensitive conditions.

bent.introLead: Beyond straight bars and mesh, CBI Tunisia extends its GFRP manufacturing platform to shaped and custom composite reinforcement elements — engineered on the same pultrusion process expertise that underpins ProBar and ProMesh.
bent.workflowIntro: Shaped composite elements are engineered through the same core production pillars applied across CBI Tunisia's GFRP platform — adapted to custom geometries rather than standard bar profiles.
bent.stage1Desc: The same precision resin control systems used across CBI Tunisia's GFRP lines govern fiber impregnation for shaped composite elements.
bent.stage2Desc: Elements are formed using CBI Tunisia's pultrusion process expertise, adapted to produce custom and shaped composite geometries.
bent.stage3Desc: Standardized quality calibration protocols validate shaped elements against the same mechanical benchmarks applied across the platform.
bent.stage4Desc: Real-time production monitoring and preventive maintenance frameworks protect consistency throughout production.
bent.diagramCaption1: Bent and shaped composite element production workflow.
bent.processPara1: Shaped and custom composite reinforcement elements draw on CBI Tunisia's advanced pultrusion process control and structured quality management systems — the same engineering discipline behind ProBar and ProMesh, applied to non-standard geometries.
bent.processPara2: Detailed dimensional and load specifications for bent elements are developed per project and available on request from CBI Tunisia's technical department, which supports project-level design and material validation directly.
bent.diagramCaption2: Quality calibration for shaped composite elements.
bent.philosophyTitle: One Platform, Extended to Custom Geometries
bent.philosophyPara1: CBI Tunisia's manufacturing philosophy — structured quality management, preventive maintenance, standardized quality assurance — is not limited to straight reinforcement bars. The same platform is engineered to be scalable and extendable to shaped and custom composite elements.
bent.philosophyPara2: That extension is backed by the same certification framework governing the whole platform: ISO 9001:2015, iTAB and EOTA membership, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB.
bent.benefit1Desc: As a GFRP composite, shaped elements share the inherent corrosion resistance of CBI Tunisia's ProBar and ProMesh product lines.
bent.benefit2Desc: Non-conductive composite material supports use in applications where steel's electrical conductivity is a liability.
bent.benefit3Desc: As with all GFRP composites, shaped elements are significantly lighter than equivalent steel components, easing handling and installation.
bent.benefit4Desc: Project-level design support and material validation from CBI Tunisia's technical team shape each element to the application's specific requirements.
bent.advantage1Desc: The same process flow optimization and quality calibration applied across CBI Tunisia's platform governs shaped element production.
bent.advantage2Desc: Civil engineering integration and specification development connect shaped-element production directly to project engineering teams.
bent.advantage3Desc: Real-time production monitoring and data-driven operational management support full process transparency.
bent.advantage4Desc: More than 10 years of hands-on GFRP manufacturing experience reduce the risk of a trial-and-error approach to custom geometries.
bent.seoTitle: Custom Composite Reinforcement Elements from CBI Tunisia
bent.seoPara1: CBI Tunisia extends its GFRP manufacturing platform beyond ProBar and ProMesh to shaped and custom composite reinforcement elements, engineered on the same optimized pultrusion technology, precision resin control and standardized quality calibration that define the company's production lines. construction.heroTitle: GFRP Reinforcement for Urban & Civil Construction
construction.introLead: Population growth and urbanization are driving sustained residential, commercial, healthcare, education and tourism construction — a pipeline where corrosion-free GFRP reinforcement supports durable, long-life structures from the outset.
construction.whyPara1: Urban development projects are built to serve decades of use — hospitals, schools, housing and commercial buildings all carry long design lives. PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered as a high-performance, corrosion-resistant alternative to conventional steel reinforcement, matching that long-term outlook from the first pour.
construction.whyPara2: Because GFRP is fully corrosion-resistant, non-conductive and chemically resistant, it removes the steel-reinforcement failure mode that most often drives long-term repair costs in reinforced concrete structures.
construction.challengesPara1: Sustained urban development — driven by population growth and urbanization — means reinforcement decisions made today carry consequences for decades of building use. Conventional steel reinforcement is vulnerable to corrosion and requires periodic repair, a recurring cost across a large, long-lived urban building stock.
construction.challengesPara2: As construction pipelines expand across residential, commercial, healthcare, education and tourism projects, reinforcement that reduces long-term maintenance exposure becomes a meaningful advantage for developers and asset owners planning for decades of use.
construction.useCasesIntro: Urban development driven by population growth and urbanization spans several construction categories:
construction.advantage1Desc: ≥1000 MPa tensile strength, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel reinforcement.
construction.advantage2Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction, versus steel's vulnerability to corrosion over a building's service life.
construction.advantage3Desc: At approximately 75% the weight of steel, easing logistics and on-site handling across large urban construction sites.
construction.advantage4Desc: Non-conductive, chemically resistant construction, compared to steel's conductivity and limited chemical resistance.
construction.performancePara1: PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered for a 75–100 year design service life, compared to 30–50 years typical of steel reinforcement — a meaningful margin for buildings designed to serve their communities for generations.
construction.performancePara2: That extended service life is backed by ISO 9001:2015 quality management, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, giving developers and specifiers a technically validated basis for long-term performance.
construction.maintenancePara1: Where steel reinforcement requires periodic repair over a structure's lifetime, GFRP reinforcement requires minimal maintenance even in aggressive environments — reducing disruption to occupied buildings such as hospitals, schools and commercial premises.
construction.maintenancePara2: Lower maintenance requirements translate into an improved total cost of ownership across the building's service life, a consideration that compounds across large-scale urban development programs.
construction.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about GFRP for urban & civil construction.
construction.faqQ1: Why choose GFRP reinforcement for urban construction projects?
construction.faqA1: Urban buildings — hospitals, schools, housing, commercial developments — carry long design lives. PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered as a corrosion-resistant alternative to steel, matching that long-term outlook from the first pour.
construction.faqQ2: What service life can urban construction projects expect?
construction.faqA2: PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered for a 75–100 year design service life, compared to 30–50 years typical of steel — a meaningful margin for buildings designed to serve their communities for generations.

infrastructure.heroTitle: GFRP Reinforcement for Public Infrastructure & Transport
infrastructure.introLead: Large-scale modernization of transport, utilities, energy and public infrastructure is generating strong, sustained demand for high-performance reinforcement — the kind of long-life public asset where PROBAR GFRP's corrosion resistance and extended service life deliver lasting value.
infrastructure.whyPara1: Public infrastructure is built to serve the public for generations, backed by sustained government-led capital investment. PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered as a high-performance, corrosion-resistant alternative to conventional steel reinforcement, suited to assets designed for very long operational lifespans.
infrastructure.whyPara2: Non-conductive, chemically resistant and fully corrosion-resistant, GFRP reinforcement is built to withstand the demanding conditions public infrastructure assets face over decades of continuous service.
infrastructure.challengesPara1: Large-scale modernization of transport, utilities, energy and public infrastructure represents sustained, government-backed capital investment with long planning horizons. Reinforcement that requires periodic repair — as conventional steel does — adds recurring cost and disruption to infrastructure that the public depends on continuously.
infrastructure.challengesPara2: Public capital expenditure provides visibility and stability to infrastructure pipelines, but that same long-term commitment raises the stakes on reinforcement durability: assets built today must perform reliably for decades without early intervention.
infrastructure.useCasesIntro: Large-scale infrastructure modernization spans several categories of public asset:
infrastructure.advantage1Desc: ≥1000 MPa tensile strength, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel reinforcement.
infrastructure.advantage2Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction, versus steel's vulnerability to corrosion.
infrastructure.advantage3Desc: At approximately 75% the weight of steel, easing logistics across large infrastructure projects.
infrastructure.advantage4Desc: Non-conductive and chemically resistant construction supports an improved total cost of ownership across long-life public infrastructure assets.
infrastructure.performancePara1: A 75–100 year design service life, compared to 30–50 years typical of steel, aligns reinforcement performance with the long operational horizons expected of transport, utilities and energy infrastructure.
infrastructure.performancePara2: That performance is backed by ISO 9001:2015, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification — a validated basis for specifying GFRP in public infrastructure programs.
infrastructure.maintenancePara1: Minimal maintenance in aggressive environments, compared to the periodic repair steel reinforcement requires, reduces the lifecycle disruption and cost associated with maintaining public infrastructure assets that must remain continuously in service.
infrastructure.maintenancePara2: For infrastructure backed by sustained public capital expenditure, lower maintenance demand supports more predictable long-term asset management.
infrastructure.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about GFRP for public infrastructure & transport.
infrastructure.faqQ1: Why is GFRP reinforcement suited to public infrastructure projects?
infrastructure.faqA1: Public infrastructure is built to serve for generations, backed by sustained capital investment. PROBAR GFRP reinforcement's corrosion resistance and extended service life align with those long operational horizons.
infrastructure.faqQ2: How does PROBAR reduce lifecycle cost on infrastructure assets?
infrastructure.faqA2: By eliminating the periodic repair conventional steel reinforcement requires, PROBAR reduces recurring maintenance cost and disruption on infrastructure the public depends on continuously.

roads.introLead: New industrial cities, economic zones and logistics hubs require substantial structural volumes for factories, warehouses and heavy facilities — exactly the high-durability, targeted application PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is engineered for.
roads.whyPara1: PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for logistics platforms — not as a universal steel replacement, but as the right choice where corrosion resistance and lifecycle cost matter most across large-scale facility construction.
roads.whyPara2: At approximately 75% the weight of steel, GFRP reinforcement reduces logistics costs and simplifies installation — a practical advantage on large industrial and logistics construction sites where structural steel volumes are substantial.
roads.challengesPara1: New industrial cities, economic zones and logistics hubs require substantial structural steel volumes for factories, warehouses and heavy facilities. At that scale, reinforcement that is heavier, more corrosion-prone and requires periodic repair compounds logistics and maintenance costs across many structures.
roads.challengesPara2: Facilities built to support logistics and industrial operations are expected to remain in continuous service — unplanned maintenance or early degradation directly affects operational uptime.
roads.useCasesIntro: Mega industrial and logistics projects span several facility types:
roads.advantage1Desc: Reduced weight lowers logistics costs and simplifies handling across large-scale factory and warehouse construction.
roads.advantage2Desc: ≥1000 MPa tensile strength, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel.
roads.advantage3Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction across large structural volumes.
roads.advantage4Desc: Non-conductive, chemically resistant construction supports an improved total cost of ownership.
roads.performancePara1: A 75–100 year design service life, against 30–50 years typical of steel, supports the continuous-operation expectations of factories, warehouses and heavy facilities.
roads.performancePara2: Backed by ISO 9001:2015, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, PROBAR gives logistics and industrial developers a validated reinforcement choice for large-scale facility construction.
roads.maintenancePara1: Minimal maintenance in aggressive environments, rather than the periodic repair steel requires, helps protect operational uptime across factories, warehouses and logistics hubs built for continuous use.
roads.maintenancePara2: Reduced maintenance demand compounds favorably at scale — a meaningful consideration across the substantial structural volumes required by new industrial cities and logistics hubs.

roads.faqQ1: Is PROBAR suitable for large-scale logistics and industrial facility construction?
roads.faqA1: Yes. PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for factories, warehouses and heavy facilities in industrial cities and logistics hubs, wherever corrosion resistance and lifecycle cost matter most.
roads.faqQ2: Does GFRP reinforcement reduce logistics costs on large projects?
roads.faqA2: At roughly 75% less weight than steel, PROBAR reinforcement simplifies handling and reduces transport and logistics costs across large-scale facility construction.

marine.heroTitle: GFRP Reinforcement for Coastal & Marine Infrastructure
marine.introLead: PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for coastal infrastructure — engineered with full corrosion resistance for structures exposed to saltwater and aggressive marine environments.
marine.whyPara1: Coastal infrastructure is named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications, precisely because it is where conventional steel reinforcement is most exposed to the conditions it handles worst: saltwater and marine chemical exposure.
marine.whyPara2: GFRP reinforcement is fully corrosion-resistant and non-conductive, removing the primary failure mode that drives deterioration and repair costs in reinforced concrete exposed to marine environments.
marine.challengesPara1: Steel reinforcement is vulnerable to corrosion, and that vulnerability is at its most severe in coastal and marine environments, where saltwater exposure accelerates deterioration and drives the periodic repair steel typically requires.
marine.challengesPara2: Coastal infrastructure is also often difficult and costly to access for maintenance and repair — making reinforcement that minimizes the need for intervention especially valuable in these environments.
marine.useCasesIntro: PROBAR is engineered for coastal infrastructure exposed to saltwater and marine conditions — a targeted application, not a general-purpose substitute for steel:
marine.advantage1Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction, directly addressing steel's core vulnerability in marine environments.
marine.advantage2Desc: High chemical resistance, compared to steel's limited resistance, for structures exposed to saltwater and marine chemical conditions.
marine.advantage3Desc: Non-conductive construction, compared to steel's conductivity, an added consideration in marine settings.
marine.advantage4Desc: ≥1000 MPa tensile strength, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel.
marine.performancePara1: A 75–100 year design service life, against 30–50 years typical of steel, is especially meaningful in marine environments, where corrosion would otherwise shorten steel's real-world performance well below its nominal design life.
marine.performancePara2: That extended, corrosion-resistant performance is backed by ISO 9001:2015, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification.
marine.maintenancePara1: GFRP reinforcement requires minimal maintenance even in aggressive environments — directly addressing the challenge steel faces in coastal and marine settings, where steel requires periodic repair driven by ongoing corrosion.
marine.maintenancePara2: For coastal assets where maintenance access is difficult or costly, reduced intervention requirements support an improved total cost of ownership over the structure's lifetime.
marine.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about GFRP for coastal & marine infrastructure.
marine.faqQ1: Why is GFRP reinforcement recommended for coastal and marine structures?
marine.faqA1: Coastal infrastructure is named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications because it's where conventional steel corrodes fastest. PROBAR GFRP reinforcement offers full corrosion resistance in saltwater and marine environments.
marine.faqQ2: How much longer does GFRP reinforcement last in marine environments than steel?
marine.faqA2: PROBAR is engineered for a 75–100 year design service life; in marine conditions this margin is especially meaningful, since saltwater exposure typically shortens steel's real-world performance well below its nominal design life.

industrial.introLead: PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for industrial facilities — engineered with chemical resistance and non-conductivity for demanding industrial environments.
industrial.whyPara1: Industrial facilities are named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications. Chemical exposure and electrical safety considerations common in industrial environments are precisely where GFRP's material properties outperform conventional steel reinforcement.
industrial.whyPara2: High chemical resistance and non-conductive construction make GFRP reinforcement well suited to industrial facilities where steel's limited chemical resistance and electrical conductivity are liabilities.
industrial.challengesPara1: Industrial facilities often involve chemical exposure and processing conditions that test the limits of conventional steel reinforcement, whose chemical resistance is limited and whose conductivity raises electrical safety considerations in some settings.
industrial.challengesPara2: Steel's vulnerability to corrosion and need for periodic repair adds recurring cost and potential operational disruption in facilities designed for continuous industrial use.
industrial.useCasesIntro: PROBAR is engineered as a targeted reinforcement solution for industrial facilities:
industrial.advantage1Desc: High chemical resistance, compared to steel's limited resistance, in demanding industrial conditions.
industrial.advantage2Desc: Non-conductive construction, compared to steel's conductivity, relevant to industrial electrical safety considerations.
industrial.advantage3Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction, versus steel's vulnerability to corrosion.
industrial.advantage4Desc: These combined properties support an improved total cost of ownership in industrial settings.
industrial.performancePara1: A 75–100 year design service life, against 30–50 years typical of steel, supports the continuous-operation demands of industrial facilities designed to run for decades.
industrial.performancePara2: That performance is backed by ISO 9001:2015, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, giving industrial developers a technically validated reinforcement choice.
industrial.maintenancePara1: Minimal maintenance in aggressive environments, rather than the periodic repair steel requires, helps protect uptime in industrial facilities where unplanned maintenance can disrupt continuous operations.
industrial.maintenancePara2: Reduced maintenance and chemical-resistant construction together support a lower total cost of ownership across the operational life of an industrial facility.
industrial.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about GFRP for industrial facilities.
industrial.faqQ1: Why use GFRP reinforcement in industrial facilities?
industrial.faqA1: Industrial facilities are named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications: chemical exposure and electrical safety considerations are precisely where GFRP's chemical resistance and non-conductivity outperform conventional steel reinforcement.
industrial.faqA2: No. Unlike steel, PROBAR GFRP reinforcement is non-conductive, an important property in industrial settings with electrical safety considerations.

water.introLead: PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for maintenance-sensitive projects — precisely where the cost and disruption of periodic steel repair matter most.
water.whyPara1: Maintenance-sensitive projects are named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications — environments where the periodic repair conventional steel reinforcement requires is costly, disruptive, or simply impractical to carry out.
water.whyPara2: GFRP reinforcement is engineered to require minimal maintenance even in aggressive environments, directly addressing the maintenance burden that makes steel reinforcement a poor fit for these projects.
water.challengesPara1: Steel reinforcement requires periodic repair over a structure's lifetime — a manageable cost in easily accessible structures, but a significant challenge where access for maintenance and repair is limited, costly, or would disrupt ongoing use.
water.challengesPara2: Every intervention required to repair corroding steel reinforcement adds cost, downtime and risk. In maintenance-sensitive settings, minimizing the frequency of intervention is often as important as the reinforcement's initial performance.
water.useCasesIntro: PROBAR is engineered as a targeted solution for maintenance-sensitive projects, wherever intervention is costly or impractical:
water.advantage1Desc: Minimal maintenance in aggressive environments, compared to the periodic repair conventional steel reinforcement requires.
water.advantage2Desc: Fully corrosion-resistant construction removes the primary driver of steel reinforcement repair.
water.advantage3Desc: Extended service life reduces the frequency of major intervention over a structure's lifetime.
water.advantage4Desc: Lower maintenance demand translates into an improved total cost of ownership.
water.performancePara1: A 75–100 year design service life, against 30–50 years typical of steel, means fewer major interventions are required over the life of the structure — directly valuable wherever maintenance access is constrained.
water.performancePara2: That performance is backed by ISO 9001:2015, European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295, EPD and CNERIB certification, giving specifiers a validated basis for choosing GFRP in maintenance-sensitive projects.
water.maintenancePara1: Minimal maintenance in aggressive environments is the core advantage PROBAR brings to maintenance-sensitive projects — reducing the frequency, cost and disruption of the repair interventions conventional steel reinforcement requires.
water.maintenancePara2: For projects where every maintenance intervention carries real cost or risk, that reduced maintenance burden is often the deciding factor in choosing GFRP over conventional steel reinforcement.
water.faqSubtitle: Questions engineers ask about GFRP for maintenance-sensitive environments.
water.faqQ1: What makes PROBAR suited to maintenance-sensitive projects?
water.faqA1: Maintenance-sensitive projects are named directly among PROBAR's targeted applications — environments where the periodic repair conventional steel requires is costly, disruptive or impractical to carry out.
water.faqQ2: How does PROBAR reduce maintenance requirements over a structure's life?
water.faqA2: With full corrosion resistance and a 75–100 year design service life against 30–50 years typical of steel, PROBAR requires fewer major interventions over the life of the structure.

faq.title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
faq.subtitle: Answers to the questions engineers, contractors and specifiers ask most about PROBAR GFRP reinforcement.
faq.a1: PROBAR is a Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) reinforcement technology — a high-performance, corrosion-resistant alternative to conventional steel reinforcement, manufactured by CBI Tunisia.
faq.q2: Does PROBAR GFRP replace steel reinforcement entirely?
faq.a2: No. PROBAR is positioned as a targeted, high-durability reinforcement solution for coastal infrastructure, industrial facilities, logistics platforms and maintenance-sensitive projects — not as a universal replacement for steel.
faq.q3: How does PROBAR GFRP compare to steel in strength and weight?
faq.a3: PROBAR GFRP delivers a tensile strength of ≥1000 MPa, compared to 400–600 MPa for conventional steel, at approximately 75% less weight — reducing logistics costs and simplifying installation.
faq.q4: What service life can I expect from PROBAR GFRP?
faq.a4: PROBAR GFRP is engineered for a 75–100 year service life, compared to 30–50 years typical of steel reinforcement, with minimal maintenance required even in aggressive environments.
faq.q5: What certifications does PROBAR / CBI Tunisia hold?
faq.a5: CBI Tunisia is ISO 9001:2015 certified, a member of iTAB and EOTA, holds European Technical Assessment ETA 24/0295 (issued 27/06/2024), and is registered under the International EPD System and CNERIB.
faq.a6: PROBAR's core product lines are ProBar (GFRP reinforcement bars) and ProMesh (GFRP mesh systems), manufactured using optimized pultrusion technology, precision resin control and standardized quality calibration protocols.
faq.q7: Do you support engineers and contractors during project design?
faq.a7: Yes. CBI Tunisia provides civil engineering integration support, technical advisory for consultants and EPC contractors, project-level design support, material validation, and specification development.
